supersedes: trades-only-btcusdt-spot-v1 (FAIL; see trades_only_v1_results.md). New hypothesis, not a retune: v1 showed about +1-2 bp gross edge at 1-5 minute fixed holds against about 24 bp round-trip cost.
hypothesis: Fewer, more selective entries on 15-60 minute signals, with rule-based exits that let winners run (up to 24h), produce mean moves per trade large enough to clear about 24 bp round-trip cost.

data_source.same_as: trades_only_v1.json data_source (daily trade zips, SHA-256 verified against .CHECKSUM, fail closed on missing days or decreasing time)

window_utc.choice: fixed before any data from 2026-10-01 onward was examined. Train overlaps v1 data (2026-09); it is diagnostics only and nothing is fitted on it. Validation and test are data no earlier experiment has looked at.

clock.time_base: exchange trade time; 1-second buckets as in v1 (bucket b holds trades with time in (b-1, b])
clock.grid: UTC 60-second grid aligned to the window start
clock.price_exit_check: every 1-second bucket, using the last trade price at or before that second

features.flow_15m: (buy_aggressor_qty - sell_aggressor_qty) / (buy_aggressor_qty + sell_aggressor_qty) over trades in (t-900s, t]; requires >= 100 trades in the window

entries.rule: at a grid time t, if flat and score(t) > threshold, buy at t + execution_delay; long or flat only, one position at a time, new signals ignored while in a position

exits.common: every position also closes at max_hold_seconds = 86400 after entry, and is force-closed at its segment end (counted as forced_exit). Exit price is the last trade at or before trigger_time + execution_delay. Price levels are measured on reference (last-trade) prices from the entry reference price, before the adverse adjustment.

rules.tp_sl: sell at the first second where price >= entry_ref * (1 + 0.0060) or price <= entry_ref * (1 - 0.0030)
rules.signal_reversal: sell at the first grid time where the entry feature's score < 0
rules.trailing_stop: sell at the first second where price <= max(price since entry) * (1 - 0.0040)
rules.fixed_4h: sell at entry + 14400s (a plain longer horizon, as a control)

configurations: 6 entries (3 candidates x 2 thresholds) x 4 exit rules = 24 configurations; this is the whole trial budget

execution_and_costs.fee_note: 0.10% per side (0.20% round trip), no verified lower fee tier
execution_and_costs.adverse_price_adjustment_breakdown: 1.0 bp half-spread + 1.0 bp slippage; entry = ref * (1 + 2bp), exit = ref * (1 - 2bp)
execution_and_costs.caveat: Same as v1: no bid/ask or depth in these files; book side is approximated from the last trade plus a fixed half-spread and slippage. Additional v2 caveat: stop-loss and trailing-stop exits are modeled as market sells 1s after the trigger at the then-last trade price; in fast moves real stop fills can be worse than this. Stop-triggered exits are counted separately so their share is visible.

chronological_split.segments: train [start, validation_start), validation [validation_start, test_start), test [test_start, end)
chronological_split.no_cross_segment_labels: positions never use prices from a later segment: they are force-closed at the segment end
chronological_split.embargo_rule: first eligible entry in validation and test is at segment_start + embargo (covers the longest feature lookback); train starts after warmup
chronological_split.train_role: in-sample diagnostics only; nothing is fitted

selection.metric: mean net return per trade after costs
selection.tie_break: more validation trades, then lower threshold, then exit rule order tp_sl, signal_reversal, trailing_stop, fixed_4h
selection.if_no_configuration_has_min_trades: nothing is selected; verdict fail; test is not run
selection.report_all_configurations: all 24 validation results are reported (multiple-comparison caveat)

test_evaluation.evaluates: the single validation-selected configuration plus baselines on the test segment
test_evaluation.enforcement: runner refuses a second test run (exclusive marker file next to the data); changing anything after seeing test results spends the test set and must be reported

baselines.no_change: constant 0 score never exceeds a positive threshold: 0 trades (identical to no_trade)
baselines.always_long_same_exit: enter at every eligible grid time when flat, with the selected configuration's exit rule (for signal_reversal: the selected feature's reversal), same costs
baselines.buy_and_hold: one round trip from the first to the last eligible time of the segment, same costs

metrics: exit_reason_counts (take_profit, stop_loss, trailing_stop, signal_reversal, time, max_hold, forced)

all_required: test mean net return per trade > 0
test t_stat of mean net return >= 2.0
test mean net return per trade > always_long_same_exit mean net return on test
pass_criteria.why_t_stat: fewer, longer trades than v1, so a positive mean alone could be luck; t >= 2 is required on the single test run
pass_criteria.otherwise: fail: stop or change the hypothesis in a new spec version; no tuning on test
pass_criteria.meaning_of_pass: evidence worth building S1 v2 around (order-book features at longer holds); not a profitability claim for live trading given the price-approximation caveat
